title: Staged read-throttling with transactional fallback protocol for downstream saturation
creator: Amina Patel
description: Problem: During cross-region surges we see downstream saturation (Redis/Kafka/Primary DB) causing tail latencies and cascading failures. Ad-hoc circuit breakers and binary fallbacks either drop valuable requests or cause inconsistent client-visible errors. Goals: 1) Introduce a staged read-throttling admission controller that enforces SLO-driven budgets per-tenant and per-query-class. 2) Provide a transactional fallback protocol for writes/reads that preserves correctness guarantees while enabling graceful degradation (soft-reads, async-apply, degraded-read-only paths). 3) Coordinate multi-region failover to prefer local-read caches, async replica reads, and probabilistic hedging only when safe. 4) Provide operator playbooks, observability, and automated rollout with canaries and kill-switches.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under synthetic downstream saturation the platform maintains 99th percentile token-gen latency SLO within configured targets for P1 tenants by shedding non-critical read classes first.
2) No data-loss for acknowledged transactional writes: writes either succeed, queue for async apply, or return a clear retryable transient response documented in API contract.
3) New admission controller exposes per-tenant token-bucket, per-route weights, and integrates with Console for real-time budgets and simulated dry-run mode.
4) Automated canary deployment across two regions with rollback on >5% regression of critical SLOs or >2x increase in error budget burn.
5) Runbook validated in chaos test that shuts down primary DB in a region and verifies fallbacks preserve correctness for high-priority tenants.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Amina: Initial spike engineering meeting. Agreed to scope phase 1 as read-only admission + async write queue. Trade-off: stronger guarantees require more state in the control plane; for phase 1 we will keep control-plane state sharded per-region to limit coupling.

2025-02-18 - Lars: Implemented token-bucket admission prototype. Observed improvement in tail latency by 28% during a synthetic Redis saturation test when non-critical reads were throttled at 30% rate. Need to tune per-route weights.

2025-02-21 - PM review (Harper Nguyen): Ensure API contract documents explicit retry semantics. Customer teams depend on HTTP 202 vs 503 distinctions. Action: add 'degraded-accepted' response code metadata and SDK helpers.

2025-02-25 - Design (Marta Li): Proposed transactional fallback variants: 1) Sync accept + enqueue apply, 2) Optimistic local-cache-read with server-side reconciliation, 3) Strong redirect to replica read for select tenants. Chosen: start with variant 1 + replica read option for read-only routes.

2025-03-01 - Reliability: ran a chaos test that killed the primary DB in eu-west while running read-heavy traffic. Observed that replica-read path reduced errors for 60% of read traffic but introduced 200ms median penalty. Decision: add region-aware hedging only above a hedge-threshold and only for routes labeled 'hedge-safe'.
2025-03-04 - Security: Kaveh requested a review for the async write queue persistence format to ensure it is encrypted at rest. Marked security_review_required.
2025-03-05 - Lars: Merged admission controller dry-run flags and console integration. Next: implement async write queue persistence and add per-tenant dashboards.
notes_and_playbook:
Operator playbook summary:
- If downstream latency climbs and error budget burn > 20% in 10m window: enable 'route-class-throttle' for non-critical classes via Console toggle.
- To force-failover of region: set region-priority=[secondary,primary] and enable async-apply drain.
- To revert: disable throttles and resume normal admission; verify P95/P99 for critical tenants.
- Debug commands: 
  * runtimectl admission status --tenant TID --route RNAME
  * runtimectl queue inspect --region eu-west --age>5m

Metrics to monitor:
- tokenbucket_fill_rate per-tenant
- admission_rejections_by_route
- async_queue_size and async_apply_latency
- replica_read_ratio and replica_read_p99
- downstream_error_budget_burn

Chaos scenarios to validate:
- Redis master saturation + network partition
- Primary DB gone: ensure transactional writes either acknowledge (queued) or return retryable code
- Cross-region cold-start: verify that hedging policy doesn't double-charge quota
